Senses.Note: Four independent works invoke the same pre-Chan ruler through distinct named stories and historical-philosophical lists.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Complete Record of Juelang Daosheng: Juelang lists the Yellow Emperor among rulers whom Zhuangzi’s writing can both grant and take away from. Juelang Daosheng owns the complete headword-bearing turn. Source text (天界覺浪盛禪師全錄).

Occurrences.Kwic: 黃帝與蚩尤。戰於涿鹿。蚩尤作大霧。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Book of Serenity: Wansong recounts the Yellow Emperor’s battle with Chiyou and the fog that occasioned the south-pointing carriage. Wansong Xingxiu owns the complete headword-bearing turn. Source text (萬松老人評唱天童覺和尚頌古從容庵錄).

Imperially Selected Recorded Sayings: the Yongzheng Emperor opens a preface by recalling the Yellow Emperor visiting Guangchengzi to ask about the Way. Yongzheng Emperor owns the complete headword-bearing turn. Source text (御選語錄).

Occurrences.Kwic: 黃帝遊于赤水，因罔象而得之
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Recorded Teaching of Shiyu Mingfang: Shiyu raises the Yellow Emperor losing the pearl at Red Water and recovering it through Wangxiang while questioning truth and falsehood. Shiyu Mingfang owns the complete headword-bearing turn. Source text (石雨禪師法檀).

Senses.Explanation: The Yellow Emperor is the ancient ruler whom Chan records invoke through visits to recluses, the south-pointing carriage, and the lost pearl at Red Water. Wansong recounts his battle with Chiyou: Chiyou makes a great fog, and the emperor’s south-pointing carriage guides the troops. The Yongzheng Emperor invokes Huangdi visiting Guangchengzi to ask about the Way as a precedent for rulers seeking instruction. Shiyu Mingfang raises the story in which Huangdi loses the bright pearl at Red Water and Wangxiang recovers it, then uses the story inside a public question about truth, falsity, concealment, and manifestation. Juelang Daosheng places him among the sage rulers whom Zhuangzi’s writing both deploys and undercuts. The Zen Yellow Emperor is therefore the named ruler as masters quote and reposition him, not an imported general biography.
